India's destiny is to become a developed civilisation with prosperity and responsibility.

This debt repayment is already offset by securities issuance, impacting no additional fiscal matters. Another item of ₹196.44 crore relates to the railway ministry and a court order. The government also highlighted its significant financial assistance to Jammu and Kashmir.

articles.title: Government mops up 31.5k cr from LIC share sale
articles.description: The government has successfully divested a 6.5% stake in LIC, generating an impressive Rs 31,552 crore. The strong demand during the offer for sale led to shares being priced at Rs 383.69 each. This monumental fundraising achievement marks the largest public offering in the history of the Indian stock market. Following this divestment, public shareholding in LIC has reached 10%, showing a significant advance ahead of the expected timeline.

articles.title: Govt mobilises Rs 31,552 crore via LIC offer for sale
articles.description: The government successfully raised ₹31,552 crore through the Life Insurance Corp of India Offer for Sale. This significant mobilization increased the public ownership of LIC to ten percent ahead of schedule. The issue saw strong participation from both retail and institutional investors. Non-retail investors subscribed more than three times their allocated portion on the first day. This successful offering marks India's largest public offering to date.

articles.title: Global Market: China stocks hold steady as gold miners gain, tech shares slip; Hong Kong dragged by insurers
articles.description: The Chinese stock market showed minimal fluctuation as gold shares increased, counteracting declines in tech. Meanwhile, Hong Kong faced market pressure as insurer stocks plummeted sharply. Investors are closely monitoring U.S.-China trade relations, with forthcoming trade data expected to shed light on China's economic condition. It is expected that policymakers will keep providing limited support to the softer segments of the economy.

articles.title: It's a secret: LIC’s unusually fast $3.3 billion deal kept bankers in dark
articles.description: LIC OFS: The Indian government raised $3.3 billion by selling additional LIC shares in the country's biggest secondary stock offering after executing a tightly guarded stake sale. Officials kept the launch secret, accelerated the timeline, and expanded the offer following strong institutional demand. The sale lifts LIC's public shareholding to 10%, meeting SEBI's listing requirement well ahead of the 2027 deadline.
